title: The edge-redundant rigidity conjecture for complete graphs in $\ell_\infty^d$
source: James Cruickshank, Sean Dewar and Derek Kitson, “Algebraic connectivity in normed spaces”, arXiv:2508.00134 (2025). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.00134), Conjecture 5.4

lanes.review: shard001-candidates-review-sol62-20261118-r1/REVIEW-369595.md (GPT-6.2 Sol, PASS; independent CNF and certificates)
lanes.final_paper_and_definition_check: final-paper-check-369595-sol62-20261119-r1/CHECK-369595.md (GPT-6.2 Sol, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; definitions FAITHFUL; revised paper used)

significance.root_decision: The complete graph K_8 is not edge-redundantly rigid in three-dimensional l-infinity space: no well-positioned placement of K_8 remains infinitesimally rigid after the removal of every single edge. This refutes the conjecture of Cruickshank, Dewar and Kitson that K_n is edge-redundantly rigid in l-infinity^d for all n >= 2d+2, at its first open case d = 3, n = 8. The proof reduces the property to a condition on the three colour classes of the framework (every colour class meets every cut twice), derives seven forbidden four-point patterns from the geometry, and shows the resulting propositional instance unsatisfiable; the certificate (12,876 steps) is checked inside the Lean kernel by a verified checker. K_9 is edge-redundantly rigid in l-infinity^3 (proved in Lean), and so is K_n for every n >= 10 (proved in the paper only).
significance.caveat: Computer-assisted: the unsatisfiability certificate is checked by a checker proved sound in Lean and evaluated in the kernel; the generated certificate modules are reproducible from the scripts and inputs in this folder. The journal version of the source (Linear Algebra Appl. 739, 2026) is unread. The extension of the positive result to n >= 10 is proved on paper only.

root_basis: Root extracted the 12 hand-written modules and the three generator scripts from the appendix, regenerated the CNF, the provenance records and the eight certificate modules (all sha256 identical to the appendix), rebuilt and kernel-checked all 20 modules from an empty directory (40 of 40 steps exit 0, object hashes identical to the author build, endpoint axioms within the allowed three; the certificate theorem uses only propext and Quot.sound), and screened the omega registry. An independent Sol referee compared every Lean definition with the source (FAITHFUL), re-verified unsatisfiability, both certificates, the seven patterns and the K_9 witness, and read the paper line by line; its editorially revised copy is the accepted paper.
